`rc` is an `int` that is either 0 or a negative `errno`. Please don't test it against `enum pldm_completion_codes`. For decoded response (not the case here where you're encoding a request, but elsewhere), you need to test both the returned value, and the `completion_code` member of the response struct.

Please fix throughout.
Done
std::array?
Updated to accept pointer to the request struct.
In-fact, shouldn't the caller just pass pointers to objects of the libpldm types through as arguments? It would seem that would save a lot of copying and tedium here.
std::array?
Done.
Updated to accept pointer to the request struct.
This sequence seems unnecessary?
Done
This looks quite tedious. Can we do better by using pointers to the libpldm types instead?
Done
See: https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/anti-patterns.md#ill-defined-data-structuring-in-lg2-message-strings
Removed cuz I don't know how to make it better for a debug log.
If this is not `PLDM_SUCCESS`, then none of the rest of the data is defined. You must test this first before accessing remaining members of the response struct.
Done
See https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/anti-patterns.md#ill-defined-data-structuring-in-lg2-message-strings
Removed cuz I don't know how to make it better for a debug log.
Recheck and remove used definitions such as TransferCtx, SectionOffset...
Moved them to the [commit](https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/pldm/+/82472) where they are used.

How about `co_return respPtr->completion_code`?

as my opinion, When there is no error in encode, send, receive, decode, the API caller will concern about the completion code instead of return code from pldm/libpldm apis.
Yes, it was a mistake. `rc` is errno and the return value here should be PLDM error code instead.

How about return?
The same comments for other APIs.

It's not the returned value of the function (which is exec::task<int>), it's the output param that the function will set value to. So, param[out] is correct. But I added @return to specify the return type.
Can we perform a null check on reqPtr before we dereference it?
Hi @pavithrabarithaya07@gmail.com, encode and decode APIs have NULL check for the in/out pointers and return error code if a NULL is passed in, do we still need to pre-check it? I genuinely wonder.
Acknowledged
here too and everywhere below?
Done

````
 *  @param[out] respPtr - pointer to the response struct
 *
 *  @return PLDM completion code
 */
 ```
 Apply the same for others descriptions.
Done

Added some comments, please check.

Please make sure to run the clang-formatter - I see many places white spaces and some alignment issues.
NIT: These names such as FD, checksum very generic and   might conflict with linux file descriptor names. Since its in namespace, that is good. But i would recommend to use PldmFd, PldmChecksum.

Checksum => CRC32Type. Because CRC32 value has to be an uint32_t, right?
FD => DfOpenFD as it belongs to DfOpen command. And it was moved to the next commit where it's actually used.
pldm_tid_t is uint8_t for which its efficient to pass by value.
Right, uint8_t would rather be passed in by value. Thanks for pointing out.
I think it's better to use "reinterpret_cast<pldm_msg*>(request.data())" which is much cleaner, Readable.
We have actually moved from that to the placement new to adhere to the C++ characteristics of this repo.
We can return the rc directly right instead of PLDM_ERROR?
encode_pldm_file_df_open_req returns errno (can be negative) but the APIs in this repo takes PLDM error code so I don't return rc here (don't be bothered by the return type exec::task<int>)

Follow the coding guidelines for variable names - In other place too.

https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/cpp-style-and-conventions.md

Thanks for noticing. However, payload_length has been used every where in the repo as the variable name of the length of payload so I want to keep them consistent, you know? Maybe a refactoring in the future can get rid of them but can we just leave it as is?
IS it file descriptor or transfer context?

MultipartReceive command das a TransferContext field in the Base spec (DSP0240) and it will be referred to as the FileDescriptor field of the DfRead command in the File Transfer spec (DSP0242). See Table 19 DfRead Command to MultipartReceive Command Mapping Format in DSP0242 v1.0.0.
NIT: Redundant with Line 271. Can be removed.
This can improve readability by separating error handling paths from the successful execution path. Therefore, keeping it as is is acceptable.
